law-of-demand.def: As the price of a good rises, the quantity buyers want falls, other things equal; the demand curve slopes downward.

quantity-demanded.def: The amount of a good buyers want at one particular price. A change in the good's own price changes the quantity demanded, a movement along the demand curve.

demand-shifter.def: Anything other than the good's own price that changes demand and shifts the curve: tastes, income (normal and inferior goods), the prices of substitutes and complements, expectations and the number of buyers.

income-substitution.def: The two reasons demand slopes down: a lower price makes the good cheaper than its alternatives (substitution effect) and raises what buyers' incomes can buy (income effect).
